summary: On-chain multi-chain ERC-20 risk assessment. Validators agree on a 32-ordinal feature vector; every score is arithmetic over it.

contract_format.notes: Two lines, version first. py-genlayer:test is a symbolic id the node resolves; pinned content hashes were tried and refused with 'invalid_contract runner malformed'. Storage lives at gl.storage.* only - a bare TreeMap[...] is a NameError on chain. UserError carries .data, not .message. See docs/PROBE.md section 12.
contract_format.sdk: genlayer-js 2.0.0-rc.1 in the frontend (first version carrying studioDevnet / chain 61997); genlayer CLI 0.40.0-rc.3

data_source: Blockscout /api/v2 for the five REST documents, plus one eth_call of owner() over JSON-RPC - publicnode first, Blockscout's own /api/eth-rpc as the fallback. All unauthenticated.
note: Verify with: shasum -a 256 build/*.min.py against the sha256 fields below, or genlayer code <address> | diff - build/TokenScope.min.py (the CLI appends trailing newlines; strip them).

TokenScope.fee_note: fee_wei set to 0 on this demo deployment. The CLI has no flag for attaching CONTRACT value to a write - --fee-value is the network fee deposit, a different thing - so a non-zero fee would make request_risk uncallable from the command line. The fee path is exercised in the offline suite.
TokenScope.verified: genlayer code <address> is byte-identical to build/TokenScope.min.py after stripping the trailing newlines the CLI adds. Checked after deploy.

studio-dev.writes_need_fees: Every write reverts with FeeValueMustBeNonZero(1) unless BOTH --fees (the distribution object) and --fee-value are supplied. tools/deploy_studio_dev.sh reads them out of `genlayer estimate-fees --json`.

adds: Deeper rug detection: HIDDEN_OWNER, UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, LOW_HOLDER_COUNT, CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY - four flags, all deterministic checks over explorer JSON, none of them asking the model anything.

Rescan and risk history: rescan_token(token_id), a previous score frozen onto every record, risk_delta, get_risk_history(token_id), get_history_by_address(token, chain, count), and a /history/[token] page.
Portfolio scanner: batch_scan(addresses, chain) over up to 5 tokens with on-chain aggregates, and a paste-addresses tab on /portfolio.
milestone.vector_change: 29 ordinals -> 32: hidden_owner, hold_lo, src_owner. _digest prefixes the hash with the canonical length, so a 1.1.0 hash (prefix 465) can never collide with a 1.0.0 one (prefix 422).
milestone.signature_change: get_risk_history now takes token_id. The address-addressed form is get_history_by_address(token_address, chain, count). RiskConsumer is unaffected - it only calls get_risk, is_safe, require_safe, check_rug_pull, get_badge and get_stats.
milestone.renames: UNVERIFIED -> UNVERIFIED_SOURCE and CONCENTRATED -> CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY, rather than adding duplicate flags that would double-count in batch_scan.total_rug_flags. CONCENTRATED_SUPPLY also moved from the 75% rung to the 50% one the name claims; the rug ladder still keys its severe rungs off 75%.

history.why_studio_dev: 1.1.0 previously ran on an older Studio network, and 1.0.0 on two networks at once. Everything now lives on one so old and new features are demonstrable in one place - which also removed the split-brain where the app read one deployment and the docs described another.
history.port_cost: The move required the v0.6 dialect: a two-line runner header, gl.contract.Contract, gl.storage.*, gl.vm.run_nondet, gl.contract.interface, and UserError.data. It moved no ordinal - USDT's content_hash is identical before and after (see cross_format_determinism).

earlier_size_finding.claim: AuditCourt's notes put the GenVM runner deploy limit at 48 KB.
earlier_size_finding.measured_2026_08_31: Stale. A 50,382-byte TokenScope artifact deployed successfully.
earlier_size_finding.measured_2026_09_02: There IS a ceiling and it was found by walking into it. A 54,325-byte artifact was refused with 'invalid transaction: BlockPubdataLimitReached' at eth_estimateGas, followed by a misleading 'intrinsic gas too low' on the send. Padded probe contracts then bracketed it: 52,000 and 53,000 both deployed, 53,700 was refused.
earlier_size_finding.why_it_matters: It is a BLOCK pubdata limit, not a per-transaction one, so the exact figure depends on what else is in the block. test/test_logic.py budgets 53,000 rather than 53,700 for that reason, and keeps doing so even where the current network prices deploys differently - a size test that only passes because today's network is generous is not a test.
earlier_size_finding.how_it_was_fixed: Not by cutting a feature. tools/minify_contract.py gained a string-pooling pass (54,325 -> 52,070) and later a scope-resolved identifier-renaming pass (59,532 -> 51,427). Neither changed any string's value, and USDT's content hash is identical before and after each.

history.retired_networks: Deploy-ceiling and CLI-compatibility measurements for the networks this project used to target are kept in docs/PROBE.md sections 11 and 12, dated, because the figures were measured rather than assumed and the method transfers. They are history, not configuration.
